sections.h2: Who values and who bills property in Rutherford County
sections.html:
Values come from the Property Assessor and bills come from the County Trustee. Each has its main office in Murfreesboro, and the Trustee keeps a second location in Smyrna.

  • Property Assessor: 615-898-7750, with an online parcel search at rcpatn.com and a drop box outside the County Office Building at 319 N. Maple St.
  • County Trustee: Murfreesboro 615-893-5210, Smyrna and Eagleville 615-898-7705. La Vergne collects its own city tax at 615-793-3388.
  • Register of Deeds: records the deeds that tell the Assessor who the new owner is.

Beyond the counters, the Trustee runs an online payment portal and a phone line. If you are selling, ask the Trustee's staff what is open on your account before you call the title company.

The county is estimated at 386,352 residents on July 1, 2025, against 341,482 at the April 2020 base, a jump of 13.1 percent. For 2020 to 2024 the median owned home was worth $382,600 and median household income was $85,470. Owners live in 64.8 percent of homes, rent at the median is $1,502, and builders pulled 3,169 permits in 2025. Incorporated places are Murfreesboro, La Vergne and Eagleville, plus the Town of Smyrna.

sections.h2: What rate do Rutherford County owners pay per $100?
sections.html:
The county levy for 2025 is $1.8762 on each $100 of assessed value. Two municipalities add their own levy: Smyrna at $0.5257 and Eagleville at $0.4051.

Owners in Smyrna and Eagleville receive a single combined bill, since the Trustee has collected for Smyrna since October 2017 and for Eagleville since October 2019. Murfreesboro and La Vergne bill separately, with their own tax pages linked from the Trustee site. A house inside either of those cities has two collectors, so request both payoff figures before closing.

Rates move from year to year, so trust the figure printed on your current bill over any older number.

Payment opens the first Monday in October and stays interest free through the last day of February. Nobody gets a discount for paying early.

You may also make partial payments, prepay, or set up monthly bank drafts. The trustee at 615-893-5210 can explain how.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Rutherford County property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay through the Trustee's online portal, by phone, at the counters or by mail. Phone payments go through 1-888-546-4299 and require a seven digit receipt number, padded with leading zeros when it is shorter.

  • In person: both offices take cash, checks, cards, money orders and cashier's checks. Write checks to Rutherford County Trustee.
  • Regular mail: PO Box 1316, Murfreesboro, TN 37133.
  • Overnight delivery: Rutherford County Trustee, Historic Courthouse, Room 102, Murfreesboro, TN 37130.
  • With every payment: add a daytime phone number and your receipt or account number.

Servicers get tax data on request, so if your lender pays from escrow the paper bill is only for your records.

sections.h2: Who is responsible for the tax bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
A new owner should read the closing statement or ask the title company who owes what, because unpaid taxes keep building against the property itself. The yearly bill spans January 1 through December 31.

Business owners follow a similar rule. A business that was operating on January 1 owes personal property tax for the full year, even if it closed before December 31. Call the County Clerk at 615-898-7800 and the Assessor at 615-898-7750 if a business has shut down.

Owners who rent a house by the night face a separate yearly filing with the Assessor, a questionnaire and affidavit due each September for the following tax year. Call the office about the current cycle.

sections.h2: How to contest a Rutherford County assessment
sections.html:
Three steps apply: an Assessor review, the local equalization board, and then the State Board of Equalization. County boards generally open their hearings on June 1.

A state filing must arrive by August 1 or within 45 days after the local board's notice, whichever is later (T.C.A. 67-5-1412(e)). Assessments reflect the situation on January 1. The Assessor's site has a presentation on property values and revaluation, so check it for the current reappraisal cycle.

sections.h2: What the register charges to file your deed
sections.html:
Deeds are billed at $5.00 a page, $10.00 minimum, plus a $2.00 computer fund fee, and the state conveyance tax is $3.70 for each $1,000. A $1.00 fee is collected only when that state tax is paid. The fee list cites T.C.A. 8-21-1001.

Staff at the Register's office do not run title searches and make no promise that a property is free and clear, so leave that step to a title company. The office also offers a MyLandAlert notice service for early warning of land fraud on your parcel.

The Trustee runs two programs, a Senior Tax Freeze and relief for disabled veteran owners and their surviving spouses, and both are limited to a primary residence.

  • Senior Tax Freeze: owners 65 and older lock the tax at the amount for the year they qualify, on up to five acres. The income limit is reset every year and you reapply each time. Remodeling raises the frozen amount, and a sale or lost eligibility puts the house back at current value and rate.
  • Veteran relief: the benefit is figured on only the first $175,000 of market value. Applications are due 35 days after the jurisdiction's delinquency date, and the tax must be paid by then.

A surviving spouse qualifies only if married to the veteran at the time of death and not remarried since.

sections.h2: Settling the bill at a Rutherford County closing
sections.html:
A sale here usually involves one county bill and, for some addresses, a city bill. Work through it in this order.

  1. Ask the Trustee at 615-893-5210 for the balance, and the city office too if the house is in Murfreesboro or La Vergne.
  2. If a lender escrows your tax, confirm with the servicer that the last payment posted.
  3. Give the title company each figure and the closing date, so it can pay from your proceeds.
  4. After closing, keep the settlement statement with your tax records.

A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is needs the same payoffs, so having them ready shortens the timeline. If a balance turns out to be larger than you expected, ask the office what it consists of before you agree to a closing date, since interest adds to it each month.

faqs.q: What is Rutherford's 2025 property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county charges $1.8762 on every $100 of assessed value. Smyrna tacks on $0.5257 and Eagleville $0.4051, while Murfreesboro and La Vergne each run their own city collection.

faqs.q: When do Rutherford County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Once February ends. The bill is payable from the first Monday in October, and each month after the delinquency date adds 1.5 percent interest to what is unpaid.

faqs.q: Does paying early earn a discount in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: No. Paying in October costs the same as paying in February, because the Trustee gives no early payment discount.

faqs.q: Who handles a value dispute in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: Start with the Property Assessor at 615-898-7750. Anything the county board leaves unsettled can go to the State Board of Equalization by the August 1 or 45 day deadline.

faqs.q: Can Rutherford County seniors freeze their tax?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are 65 or older, live in the house and have no more than five acres, and you reapply every year. The Trustee at 615-898-7705 can quote this year's income limit.
